en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighth Chapter
Discussion on the Intermediate State:
Is there an intermediate state?
Yes, there is.
Is it the case that there is sensual existence (*kāmabhava*)? One should not say so … [and so on] … Is it the case that there is intermediate existence (*antarābhava*)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is it the existence of form (rūpabhava)? You should not say so …pe…
Is there an intermediate state (antarābhava)?
Yes. Is it an immaterial existence (arūpabhava)? [No.]
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there an intermediate existence (antarābhava)? Yes.
Is there an intermediate existence between the sensual existence and the fine-material existence?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is there an intermediate existence?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is there an intermediate existence between the fine-material existence and the immaterial existence?
You should not speak thus… [and so on].
Is there no intermediate existence between the sense-sphere existence (*kāmabhava*) and the fine-material existence (*rūpabhava*)?
Yes.
If there is indeed no intermediate existence between the sense-sphere existence and the fine-material existence, then, alas, you should not say: [that there is an intermediate existence].
“There is an intermediate state. Is it not the case that there is no intermediate state between the form existence (*rūpa-bhava*) and the formless existence (*arūpa-bhava*)?
Yes, it is so.
If there is no intermediate existence between the form realm (rūpabhava) and the formless realm (arūpabhava), then indeed, it should not be said:
"There is an intermediate existence.
Is there an intermediate existence?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that fifth *yoni* (mode of birth), that sixth *gati* (destination), that eighth *viññāṇaṭṭhiti* (station of consciousness), and that tenth *sattāvāsa* (abode of beings)?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is there an intermediate state (antarābhava)? Yes.

Is the intermediate state a becoming (bhava), a destination (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a womb (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti), and the acquisition of a personal existence (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the intermediate state?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
Is it the case that there are beings who go to the intermediate state (*antarābhava*)?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...do beings in the intermediate state take birth, grow old, die, pass away, and reappear?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there,
in the intermediate state, form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
Is the intermediate state (antarābhava) a five-aggregate existence (pañcavokārabhava)?
One should not say so… [as before]… Is there sensual existence (kāmabhava),

and is sensual existence an existence, a destiny (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a matrix (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti), and an acquisition of individuality (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Is there an intermediate state (*antarābhava*), and is that intermediate state a state of existence (*bhava*), a destination (*gati*), an abode of beings (*sattāvāsa*), cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*), a womb (*yoni*), a station of consciousness (*viññāṇaṭṭhiti*), and the acquisition of a personal identity (*attabhāvapaṭilābha*)?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the realm of sense-desire?
Yes. Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the intermediate state? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that there are beings who have entered into sensual existence? Yes.
Is it the case that there are beings who go to the intermediate state (*antarābhava*)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Are beings born,
age, die, pass away, and re-arise in the sense-sphere existence (*kāmabhava*)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are beings born, grow old, die, pass away, and reappear in the intermediate state?
You should not speak thus …pe…
In the realm of sense-desire (kāmabhava), are there form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
Yes. Are there form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness in the intermediate state (antarābhava)? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is sensual existence (kāmabhava) fivefold existence (pañcavokārabhava)? Yes.
Is the intermediate state (*antarābhava*) a five-aggregate existence (*pañcavokārabhava*)?
One should not say so... [and so forth] ...

Is there a fine-material existence (*rūpabhava*), and is that fine-material existence an existence, a destination (*gati*), an abode of beings (*sattāvāsa*), saṃsāra, a womb (*yoni*), a station of consciousness (*viññāṇaṭṭhiti*), and the acquisition of a personal identity (*attabhāvapaṭilābha*)?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Is there an intermediate state (antarābhava); is the intermediate state a state of existence (bhava), a destination (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a womb (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti), and the acquisition of a personal identity (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the realm of form?
Yes. Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the intermediate state? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there a being who has gone to the form-existence (rūpa-bhava)? Yes.
Is it the case that there are beings who pass into the intermediate state (*antarābhava*)?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...do beings in the realm of form (*rūpabhava*) take birth, age, die, pass away, and reappear?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are beings born, age, die, pass away, and reappear in the intermediate state?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
In the form existence (rūpabhava), are there form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
Yes. Are there form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness in the intermediate existence (antarābhava)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the existence in the realm of form (rūpabhava) the five-aggregate existence (pañcavokārabhava)? Yes.
Is the intermediate state (antarābhava) a five-aggregate existence (pañcavokārabhava)?
One should not say so... [and so forth] ...

Does immaterial existence (arūpabhava) exist? Is immaterial existence an existence, a destination (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a matrix (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti), or an acquisition of individuality (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Is there an intermediate state (antarābhava); is the intermediate state an existence (bhava), a destination (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a womb (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti), and the acquisition of a personal identity (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the formless realm?
Yes. Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the intermediate state? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that there are beings who go to the formless existence? Yes.
Is it the case that there are beings who go to the intermediate state (*antarābhava*)?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...do beings in the formless realm (*arūpabhava*) take birth, age, die, pass away, and re-arise?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Are beings born, grow old, die, pass away, and reappear in the intermediate state?
“One should certainly not say so,” … [and so on].
In the formless realm, are there feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness?
Yes. Are there feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness in the intermediate state?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is formless existence (arūpabhava) fourfold existence (catuvokārabhava)? Yes.
Is the intermediate state (*antarābhava*) an existence consisting of four aggregates (*catuvokārabhava*)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Does the intermediate state exist?
“Yes.
“Then you must say that there is an intermediate state for all beings?
“One should not speak thus…” [and so on].
Is it the case that for all beings there is no intermediate state (*antarābhava*)? Yes.
If indeed for all beings there is no intermediate state, then surely you should not say:
“There is an intermediate state.
Is there an intermediate state? Yes.
Is there an intermediate state for a person who has committed an immediate offense?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is there no intermediate state for a person who has committed an immediate offense? One should not say so.
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If there is no intermediate state for a person who has committed an act of immediate retribution, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘There is an intermediate state.’”
Is there an intermediate existence for a person who has committed an immediate offense?
Yes. Is there an intermediate existence for a person who has committed an immediate offense? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that for a person who has committed an immediate offense (*ānantariya*), there is no intermediate existence (*antarābhava*)?
Yes, it is so.
Is it not the case that for a person who has committed an immediate offense (ānantariya-kamma), there is no intermediate state (antarābhava)?
One should not say so …pe… [and likewise] for a person who is destined for hell …pe….
Is there an intermediate existence for a person who has attained the state of non-percipient beings …pe… or for a person who has attained the formless realm?
One should not say so …pe….
Is it not the case that for a person who has attained the formless realm there is no intermediate existence?
Yes, it is.
If indeed for a person who has attained the formless realm there is no intermediate existence, then certainly you should not say—
“There is an intermediate state.
Is it not the case that for a person who has attained the formless realm there is no intermediate state?
Yes, it is.
Is there an intermediate existence for a person who has gone to the formless realm?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...is there no intermediate existence for a person who has gone to the formless realm?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is it not the case that for a person who has attained the formless realm there is no intermediate existence?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is it not to be said that there is an intermediate state (antarābhava)?
Yes. But is it not the case that there is a person who attains parinirvāṇa in the interval (antarāparinibbāyī)?
“Yes.
“If there is a person who attains parinirvāṇa in the interval, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
‘There is an intermediate state.’”
If it is admitted that there is a person who attains Nibbāna in the interval, does it follow that there is an intermediate existence (*antarābhava*)? Yes.
If it is admitted that there is a person who attains Nibbāna upon landing (*upahacca*), does it follow that there is a "landing-existence" (*upahaccabhava*)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Given that there is a person who attains parinirvāṇa in the interval, does it follow that there is an intermediate state (antarābhava)? Yes.

If one accepts that there is a person who attains final nibbāna without exertion (*asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī*) … and a person who attains final nibbāna with exertion (*sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī*), must it then be said that there is existence with exertion (*sasaṅkhārabhava*)?
One should not say so … [and so on].
The Discussion on the Intermediate State is finished.
